residuals.target: Charles Elcock to D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson, ms21974-ms21975, 6-8 March 1884
residuals.secure_public_result: The St Andrews item record identifies two autograph letters signed plus one rubbing. It explicitly says the main theme is archaeological/antiquarian discussion of a medal allegedly found in a peat bog at Oughterard, County Kildare; the record separately notes natural-history discussion and references to Challenger expedition samples.
residuals.correction_to_working_expectation: The public record does not present these as primarily Challenger letters. Challenger is an explicit referenced topic within a broader correspondence item. The existence of the reference is secure; the transaction/workflow content is not.
still_open: who supplied or forwarded the samples
relation to surviving Elcock Challenger material or Type Slides
residuals.next: Request/read page images of ms21974-ms21975 only. Do not continue generic Elcock/St Andrews web discovery.
residuals.grade: S archive-item metadata; OPEN transaction content

residuals.target: Francis Maitland Balfour surviving Zeiss objectives
residuals.secure_public_result: ZEISS publishes historical production/dispatch lists for microscope stands and records recipient, delivery place, accessories, delivery date and production data. The public lists are organized around microscope/stand serial numbers; the Balfour problem concerns engraved numbers on individual surviving objectives (573, 1295, 710, 780, 542). No public indexed source found in this pass converts those objective engravings into a dispatch record.
residuals.guard: Do not feed the objective engravings into stand-number tables as if the numbering systems were identical. A microscope dispatch entry might list objectives as accessories, but that requires a recipient/stand-level hit or archive guidance.
residuals.still_open: Exact physical-lens provenance/dispatch identity beyond the already closed printed designation-level use record.
residuals.next: Archive query to ZEISS with Balfour/Cambridge plus the five objective engravings, asking whether accessory/objective registers or stand dispatch entries preserve those numbers. No more generic serial-number web searching.
residuals.grade: S publication-designation layer; exact-lens identity archive-only

residuals.target: John Thomas Norman 1872 catalogue to St Andrews surviving slides
residuals.secure_public_result: St Andrews confirms the 1872 catalogue of 2,584 mounts and a Norman group within the Bell-Pettigrew collection. The catalogue record says the Norman slides remain in situ, scattered among the slide sleeves. The parent collection preserves original sleeve/pigeon-hole ordering and multiple label layers. The public Norman group exposes no usable numeric extent and no indexed child-item list from which a 2,584-row crosswalk can be built.
residuals.guard: Do not manufacture an item crosswalk from taxonomy, label presence or group membership. Norman labels can also represent business stock or secondary commercial circulation, including slides sold after John Thomas Norman's lifetime.
residuals.still_open: Complete Norman item/export list with current addresses, label transcriptions and preferably images.
residuals.next: Proceed only after St Andrews supplies/export exposes the item layer. Until then collection-level chain remains the terminal public claim.
residuals.grade: A+/S collection-level chain; item identity blocked by data granularity

newly_closed_in_residual_pass.target: Naples catalogue offering 383 to St Andrews BPM/1/T8/6
newly_closed_in_residual_pass.result: The locally held primary OCR on printed p.253 reads 382 Delphinus phocaena L. Milz; 383 ditto ditto Penis; 384 ditto ditto Hode; 385 ditto ditto Niere. Thus offering 383 is Delphinus phocaena L., Penis. St Andrews BPM/1/T8/6 independently carries Naples Station labels, taxon Delphinus phocaena, and the right-label transcription 'Panis 383'. Station + taxon + exact number closes the surviving object as an instance corresponding to catalogue offering 383; Panis/Penis is retained as a one-letter source/transcription discrepancy.
newly_closed_in_residual_pass.guard: Catalogue offering identity does not establish manufacture date, preparator, price or identity with a particular 1880/1881 shipment copy.

operational_conclusion.meaning: The active internet discovery loop is closed. Four remaining edges are exact source-access problems; Naples 383 has moved out of the request queue through a local primary-source closure.
operational_conclusion.stop_rule: Do not reopen broad web searching for any residual target unless a requested source returns a new name, identifier, station, catalogue number or institutional address that creates a genuinely new bounded query.
